+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas
+contour construction and measurability proof are in
+\Cref*{sec:estimator-atlas-supp} of the supplementary material.
+
+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[
+ s_{\eta,0}(k)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
+\tag{3.19}
+\]
+and set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside \(\mathcal E_0\).  Partition it according to
+\((\eta,\delta)\), and define its empirical Schur complement by
+\[
+ J_N(\eta)=
+ \begin{cases}
+ I_{\delta\delta,N}-I_{\delta\eta,N}
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta,N},
+ &\eta\in\mathcal E_0,\ \lambda_{\min}(I_{\eta\eta,N})>0,\\
+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\tag{3.20}
+\]
+Let \(\widehat\eta_N\) be the recurrence fit and
+\(\mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
+J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}\).  On \(\mathcal G_N\), put
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ Z_N&=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
+ -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}
+ s_{\rm nuis}(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)\right]}
+ {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}},\\
+ \phi_N&=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.21}
+\]
+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default
+nonrejection.  These gates are uniformly asymptotically inactive.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+

+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[

+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);

+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,

+\tag{3.18}
+\]

+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}

+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have

+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[

+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.

+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}

+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+

+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas
+contour construction and measurability proof are in
+\Cref*{sec:estimator-atlas-supp} of the supplementary material.
+
+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[
+ s_{\eta,0}(k)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
+\tag{3.19}
+\]
+and set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside \(\mathcal E_0\).  Partition it according to
+\((\eta,\delta)\), and define its empirical Schur complement by
+\[
+ J_N(\eta)=
+ \begin{cases}
+ I_{\delta\delta,N}-I_{\delta\eta,N}
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta,N},
+ &\eta\in\mathcal E_0,\ \lambda_{\min}(I_{\eta\eta,N})>0,\\
+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\tag{3.20}
+\]
+Let \(\widehat\eta_N\) be the recurrence fit and
+\(\mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
+J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}\).  On \(\mathcal G_N\), put
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ Z_N&=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
+ -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}

+ {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}},\\
+ \phi_N&=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.21}
+\]
+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default
+nonrejection.  These gates are uniformly asymptotically inactive.

+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas
+contour construction and measurability proof are in
+\Cref*{sec:estimator-atlas-supp} of the supplementary material.
+
+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[
+ s_{\eta,0}(k)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
+\tag{3.19}
+\]
+and set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside \(\mathcal E_0\).  Partition it according to
+\((\eta,\delta)\), and define its empirical Schur complement by
+\[
+ J_N(\eta)=
+ \begin{cases}
+ I_{\delta\delta,N}-I_{\delta\eta,N}
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta,N},
+ &\eta\in\mathcal E_0,\ \lambda_{\min}(I_{\eta\eta,N})>0,\\
+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\tag{3.20}
+\]
+Let \(\widehat\eta_N\) be the recurrence fit and
+\(\mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
+J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}\).  On \(\mathcal G_N\), put
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ Z_N&=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
+ -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}

+ {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}},\\
+ \phi_N&=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.21}
+\]
+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default
+nonrejection.  These gates are uniformly asymptotically inactive.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

+\cite{GillKeiding2010RenewalSampling,ZhaoNagaraja2011WindowCensoredRenewal}.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+

+They also justify the uniform quadratic-mean expansions and dominated
+differentiation of \(\mu_q\), which give \textup{(U1a)}.

+\subsection{Recurrence estimator and residualized statistic}
+
+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas
+contour construction and measurability proof are in
+\Cref*{sec:estimator-atlas-supp} of the supplementary material.
+
+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[
+ s_{\eta,0}(k)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
+\tag{3.19}
+\]
+and set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside \(\mathcal E_0\).  Partition it according to
+\((\eta,\delta)\), and define its empirical Schur complement by
+\[
+ J_N(\eta)=
+ \begin{cases}
+ I_{\delta\delta,N}-I_{\delta\eta,N}
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta,N},

+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\tag{3.20}

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+

+\subsection{Recurrence estimator and residualized statistic}
+
+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas
+contour construction and measurability proof are in
+\Cref*{sec:estimator-atlas-supp} of the supplementary material.
+
+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[
+ s_{\eta,0}(k)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
+\tag{3.19}
+\]
+and set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside \(\mathcal E_0\).  Partition it according to
+\((\eta,\delta)\), and define its empirical Schur complement by
+\[
+ J_N(\eta)=
+ \begin{cases}
+ I_{\delta\delta,N}-I_{\delta\eta,N}
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta,N},
+ &\eta\in\mathcal E_0,\ \lambda_{\min}(I_{\eta\eta,N})>0,\\
+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\tag{3.20}
+\]
+Let \(\widehat\eta_N\) be the recurrence fit and
+\(\mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
+J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}\).  On \(\mathcal G_N\), put
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ Z_N&=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
+ -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}
+ s_{\rm nuis}(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)\right]}
+ {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}},\\
+ \phi_N&=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.21}
+\]
+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default
+nonrejection.  These gates are uniformly asymptotically inactive.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.
+

+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},

+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and

+\tag{3.18}

+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}

+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have

+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[

+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}

+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[
+ N^{-3/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}B_q(G_j)=o_P(1)
+\]
+uniformly.  These conclusions hold jointly and apply to the score, stopped
+Hessian, and third-order likelihood remainder under bounded root-\(N\) local
+triangular arrays.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Plug-in equicontinuity.}
+On the canonically ordered collision stratum, write the one-cycle null scores
+as \(s_\eta\) and \(s_\delta\), and define
+\[
+ \psi_\eta=s_\delta-I_{\delta\eta}I_{\eta\eta}^{-1}s_\eta,
+ \qquad
+ \Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)=N^{-1/2}
+ \sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\psi_\eta(G_j).
+\]
+For every fixed \(L<\infty\),
+\[
+ \sup_\eta\sup_{\|\eta'-\eta\|\le L/\sqrt N}
+ |\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta')-\Delta_{{\rm eff},N}(\eta)|
+ =o_{P_{\eta,0}}(1).
+\]
+The conclusion also holds under bounded contiguous local alternatives.  The
+empirical calendar information and its Schur complement, evaluated anywhere
+in the same root-\(N\) ball, converge uniformly to \(I_n(\eta)\) and
+\(J_n(\eta)\).  Hence any measurable root-\(N\) null fit may be inserted in
+the standardized efficient central sequence with an \(o_P(1)\) change.

23 1. Introduction

24 A stationary renewal record observed through a deterministic calendar window does
25 not consist of a deterministic number of complete cycles. The first and last cycles
26 are censored, the number of intervening cycles is random, and a window may contain
27 no renewal. These features are harmless for many first-order calculations, but they
28 matter when an i.i.d. Palm argument is used as a substitute for the actual experiment.
29 Conditioning a prescribed number of cycles to fit in the window is not legitimate: it
30 changes their joint law.
31 Our first result removes that boundary-cycle problem at the level of statistical
32 experiments. Given a stationary renewal window of length N , one kernel extracts
33 the first mN = N/µ0-N  complete interarrivals, where 1/2 <  < 1. In the reverse
34 direction, a kernel uses the supplied Palm sample and appends base-law cycles after
35 it is exhausted. The two couplings fail only if the record contains too few complete
36 cycles, or if generation in the reverse direction needs more than the supplied cycles
37 plus a short base-law continuation. Hellinger locality controls that continuation.
38 Both deficiency directions therefore vanish uniformly, without conditioning Palm
39 gaps on fitting inside the window.

                                                         2
The equivalence theorem is useful beyond a parametric model. Bounded-loss pro- 40

cedures transfer in both directions, information per calendar unit is Palm information 41

divided by mean cycle length, and an i.i.d. canonical-gradient variance is multiplied 42

by mean cycle length. The same statements remain valid for a fixed local cone or 43

constrained local subset, with efficiency and minimax bounds interpreted in that 44

restricted experiment. This qualification is essential at a singular boundary.  45

   Three ingredients make the singular conclusion statistically complete. First, the 53
sampled survival tail is a confluent exponential-polynomial sequence whose minimal 54

derivative has its own order-two pole. After sampling, their distinguishing compo- 58

77 [2, 12]. Finite-mixture work shows that collision rates depend on the particular
78 singularity structure [3, 7, 10].

+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas

+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[

+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.

+\[

+ \phi_N&=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.21}
+\]
+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default
+nonrejection.  These gates are uniformly asymptotically inactive.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
+
+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Stopped-score CLT and information LLN.}
+Let \(\mathcal Q\) be compact and let the integer Palm gaps \(G\) have full
+support, a common exponential moment, and parameter-continuous masses.  Let a
+stationary binary renewal record of length \(N\) contain \(K_N\) complete
+gaps, with initial forward recurrence \(A_N\) and terminal backward recurrence
+\(R_N\), and put \(D=G+1\), \(\mu_q=\EE_qD\).  Uniformly in
+\(q\in\mathcal Q\), and for triangular arrays \(q_N\in\mathcal Q\),
+\[
+ K_N=N/\mu_{q_N}+O_{P_{q_N}}(\sqrt N),\qquad
+ \max\{A_N,R_N,G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\}=O_{P_{q_N}}(\log N).
+\]
+If \(b_q(G)\in\RR^d\) is parameter-continuous, \(\EE_qb_q(G)=0\), and is
+bounded by a common polynomial in \(G\), then
+\[
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q}d_{\rm BL}\!\left(
+ \mathcal L_q\!\left[N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}b_q(G_j)\right],
+ \mathcal N_d\!\left(0,\mu_q^{-1}\EE_q[b_qb_q^\top]\right)
+ \right)\longrightarrow0.
+\]
+For every similarly dominated matrix reward \(H_q\),
+\[
+ N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}H_q(G_j)
+ -\mu_q^{-1}\EE_qH_q(G)\longrightarrow0
+\]
+uniformly in probability.  If \(B_q\) has a common polynomial envelope, then
+\[

496 6. Discussion and relation to prior work

497 Two-sided deficiency convergence strengthens the classical calendar-time information
498 calculation for stationary renewal sampling [6, 17]. It shows that the Palm and
499 stationary-window experiments have asymptotically the same bounded-loss decision
500 problems, not merely matching Fisher information. The effective sample-size conver-
501 sion then yields Palm information divided by mean cycle length and multiplies an
502 i.i.d. canonical-gradient covariance by that mean.
503 At the collision boundary, the ambient DQM chart determines the information
504 matrix while the half-space Rn-1 × [0, ) determines the decision problem. This
505 distinction explains both the one-sided Gaussian power envelope and the need to
506 interpret efficiency and minimax bounds inside the fixed constrained experiment [4,
507 15].

+
+\begin{estimator}[Measurable sampled-tail recurrence estimator]
+\label{est:serial-collision-recurrence-main}
+Delete the two incomplete endpoint cycles and let
+\(G_1,\ldots,G_{K_N}\) be the complete zero-run gaps.  Form
+\[
+ \widehat S_k=K_N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}\mathbf1_{\{G_j\ge k\}},
+ \qquad0\le k\le2n-1,
+\tag{3.17}
+\]
+with fixed values when \(K_N=0\).  Solve the empirical Hankel recurrence on
+its nonsingular gate, use a fixed fallback otherwise, and select measurably
+from a finite analytic contour atlas separating the unique two-root cluster
+from the \(n-2\) simple roots.  In the cluster, use its elementary symmetric
+coordinates and transform them analytically to \((c,\widetilde\delta)\);
+set \(\widehat\delta=(\widetilde\delta)^+\).  The resulting estimators are
+total and Borel measurable and satisfy, uniformly over the compact stratum and
+bounded local alternatives,
+\[
+ \widehat\eta_N-\eta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}),\qquad
+ \widehat\delta_N-\delta_N=O_P(N^{-1/2}).
+\tag{3.18}
+\]
+The pair \(\widehat c_N\pm\sqrt{\widehat\delta_N}\), together with the
+canonically ordered simple-rate estimates, gives \textup{(3.13)}.
+\end{estimator}
+
+The finite vector of empirical tail coordinates is root-\(N\), and
+invertibility from \Cref{prop:serial-tail-coordinates-main} gives root-\(N\)
+recurrence coefficients.  Simple roots and the two-root cluster have
+compatible analytic charts, while \((c,\delta)\) are regular analytic cluster
+coordinates.  Projection onto \([0,\infty)\) is nonexpansive, and
+\(|\sqrt{x^+}-\sqrt y|\le\sqrt{|x-y|}\) for \(y\ge0\).  The finite-atlas
+contour construction and measurability proof are in
+\Cref*{sec:estimator-atlas-supp} of the supplementary material.
+
+For the collision test, write the null one-cycle score as
+\[
+ s_{\eta,0}(k)=
+ \begin{pmatrix}s_{\rm nuis}(k;\eta)\\s_\delta(k;\eta)\end{pmatrix}.
+\]
+Fix a compact null-coordinate neighbourhood \(\mathcal E_0\) whose interior
+contains the stratum projection and whose closure lies in the common score
+chart.  For \(\eta\in\mathcal E_0\), define the empirical calendar information
+\[
+ I_N(\eta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ s_{\eta,0}(G_j)s_{\eta,0}(G_j)^\top,
+\tag{3.19}
+\]
+and set \(I_N(\eta)=0\) outside \(\mathcal E_0\).  Partition it according to
+\((\eta,\delta)\), and define its empirical Schur complement by
+\[
+ J_N(\eta)=
+ \begin{cases}
+ I_{\delta\delta,N}-I_{\delta\eta,N}
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}^{-1}I_{\eta\delta,N},
+ &\eta\in\mathcal E_0,\ \lambda_{\min}(I_{\eta\eta,N})>0,\\
+ 0,&\text{otherwise}.
+ \end{cases}
+\tag{3.20}
+\]
+Let \(\widehat\eta_N\) be the recurrence fit and
+\(\mathcal G_N=\{\widehat\eta_N\in\mathcal E_0,
+J_N(\widehat\eta_N)>0\}\).  On \(\mathcal G_N\), put
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ Z_N&=\frac{N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{K_N}
+ \left[s_\delta(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)
+ -I_{\delta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)
+ I_{\eta\eta,N}(\widehat\eta_N)^{-1}
+ s_{\rm nuis}(G_j;\widehat\eta_N)\right]}
+ {\sqrt{J_N(\widehat\eta_N)}},\\
+ \phi_N&=\mathbf1_{\{Z_N>z_{1-\alpha}\}}.
+\end{aligned}
+\tag{3.21}
+\]
+The score-chart, singular-block, and nonpositive-Schur-complement gates make
+the construction total: off \(\mathcal G_N\), set \(\phi_N=0\), the default
+nonrejection.  These gates are uniformly asymptotically inactive.

 \section{Proof of the limit-experiment theorem}
 
+The proof uses the following exact supplementary inputs.  Their proofs are
+\Cref*{lem:uniform-sampled-bin-tail-score-main,lem:uniform-stopped-renewal-score-main,lem:efficient-score-plugin-main}
+of the supplementary material.

+\smallskip\noindent\textbf{DQM and envelope.}
+For fixed \(n,\varepsilon,M,c_0\), and \(\Delta\tau>0\), there is a common
+physical one-sided neighbourhood \(\mathcal Q^+\) of
+\(\mathcal C_n(\varepsilon,M,c_0)\), in the coordinates
+\(q=(\eta,\delta)\), on which \(c\pm\sqrt\delta>0\) and, for every
+multi-index \(a\),
+\[
+\begin{aligned}
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log g_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le3,\\
+ \sup_{q\in\mathcal Q^+}|\partial_q^a\log S_q(k)|
+ &\le C_a(1+k)^{2|a|},&& 1\le|a|\le2.
+\end{aligned}
+\]
+All parameter derivatives extend continuously to \(\delta=0\), and
+\(g_q(k)\le C(1+k)^{n-1}r^k\) for a common \(r<1\).  Writing
+\(e_q(a)=S_q(a)/\mu_q\), the families \(g_q\) and \(e_q\) are uniformly
+differentiable in quadratic mean.  Uniformly over base points on the collision
+stratum and bounded physical root-\(N\) local arrays \(q_N\),
+\[
+ H^2(g_{q_N},g_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ H^2(e_{q_N},e_{q_0})=O(N^{-1}),\qquad
+ |\mu_{q_N}-\mu_{q_0}|=O(N^{-1/2}).
+\]
